newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian FM sees investors eyeing more stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian FM sees investors eyeing more stocks.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Monday that he understood that investor interest in two groups of less actively traded stocks was growing.
"I am told that the interests of investors are improving in the B1 and B2 shares," Chidambaram said after inaugurating a nationwide communication network at the Delhi Stock Exchange.
A recent surge in Indian share prices has been attributed to greater liquidity and growing investor confidence in the economy.
On Monday the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index closed 118.03 points higher at 4,465.37, a new 34-month high, piercing 4,450 for the first time since September 1994.

Chidambaram said improved technology and higher efficiency resulting from computer networks were expected to spur investor confidence in Indian stocks and called for closer coordination between stock exchanges.
"Not only the Delhi exchange but every exchange in India must work at improving the confidence (of investors)," he said.
